title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Prohibition on Large Institutional Investor Purchases of Single-Family Homes
pass_4_primary_concern: The notice does not adequately connect its numerical safe harbors, land-value formula, and phased implementation plan to evidence, fallback methods, or monitoring controls.
pass_5_high_stakes_domain_reason: The proposal affects housing access, ownership structures, renters, housing supply, and civil penalties.
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal is structurally coherent, but its numerical safe harbors, cross-jurisdiction valuation method, and phased implementation are not fully supported by evidence or a monitoring and correction framework.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: Entities and consumers may face inconsistent exception eligibility, transaction delay, or compliance costs before Treasury has tested fallback methods and implementation controls.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal creates meaningful compliance and penalty consequences while presenting mostly qualitative evidence that the selected definitions will reduce disruption and improve housing outcomes.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask Treasury to connect the burden and benefit claims to affected-entity and transaction evidence.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The clarity objective is plausible, but the record does not demonstrate that the chosen thresholds and safe harbors are the least disruptive way to operationalize the statutory exceptions.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Compare the proposal with fallback, phased, and alternative-threshold designs.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal relies on consistent administration across layered ownership structures and local valuation systems while acknowledging that tax-assessed land values may be unavailable, stale, limited, appealed, or not separately stated.

evidence.section: II.B.4 Purchase Price of the Single-Family Home
evidence.quote_or_absence: The notice recognizes that assessment practices vary and that relevant land values may not be current or available, but the proposed regulatory text supplies no complete fallback hierarchy.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Request fallback valuation rules, jurisdictional examples, and implementation testing before the effective date.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal depends on links among Treasury enforcement, HUD reporting, FHA county limits, local tax assessments, and later rulemakings, but the supplied record does not describe how those interfaces will operate during the first phase.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask Treasury to identify data owners, timing, and interim procedures for each external dependency.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The notice identifies market disruption, circumvention, consumer, and community concerns, but it does not define measurable indicators for when those risks are occurring or worsening.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Request operational indicators and reporting for disruption, exception use, and consumer effects.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The notice discusses benefits and limited recordkeeping burden but does not quantify the full effects of transaction delay, legal review, structuring changes, renter outcomes, or community distribution.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Provide impact evidence and request sensitivity analysis in the final rule.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal supplies many definition-level questions but does not establish a monitoring, correction, or public-feedback framework for inconsistent exception decisions during the phased implementation.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The notice says future rulemakings may address compliance procedures, reporting and recordkeeping, and enforcement, but the available record does not describe interim safeguards or correction procedures for the first phase.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask Treasury to publish examples, transition rules, review contacts, error-correction procedures, and public metrics before implementation.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal places documentation, valuation, and transaction-planning work on market participants, while the broader distribution of those costs across smaller entities, renters, and communities is not developed.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Request entity-size and transaction-type analysis of compliance and delay costs.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The notice expects entities relying on exceptions to maintain records but does not prescribe a retention period or routine submission, leaving future auditability dependent on private records and later enforcement procedures.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for minimum retention, accessibility, and transfer requirements proportionate to the exception claimed.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Transaction and compliance costs may arise before later procedures and enforcement guidance are adopted, but the record does not include a transition or correction mechanism for early implementation errors.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Request transition relief and a prompt correction channel for good-faith uncertainty.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal clarifies that one purchase involving multiple investors is one maximum-penalty violation but leaves responsibility allocation and the treatment of complex affiliate participation for future action.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask Treasury to distinguish minor documentation errors, serious evasion, and deliberate prohibited purchases.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Terms such as property control right, reasonably designed and implemented, material deficiency, temporary and incidental, and any other type of income or financial gain can determine whether a transaction qualifies for an exception without a complete set of examples or neutral safe harbors.

evidence.section: II.B.2, II.C, II.K, and proposed sections 36.3 and 36.15
evidence.quote_or_absence: The notice invites comments on whether the definitions are overinclusive or underinclusive, but the available record does not provide a comprehensive example set or fallback decision process for close cases.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Submit concrete edge cases and request objective examples, review standards, and anti-arbitrariness controls.
